claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi alloy has a coarse dual-phase fcc/B2 lamellar microstructure with an inter-lamellar spacing of about 2 μm.
The initial alloy undergoes catastrophic interfacial cracking and has low ductility during room-temperature tension.
Hot rolling or forging at 900–1000 °C with more than 80% reduction, followed by annealing at 600–700 °C, is an appropriate HITM schedule for this alloy.
Deformation at 900–1000 °C, above 500 MPa and at a strain rate of 10^-2 to 10^-1 s^-1 will induce dynamic recrystallization and lamellar refinement.
The proposed HITM treatment will transform the coarse lamellae into a patterned ultra-fine or nanolamellar configuration.
The transformed structure will contain alternating fcc and B2 phases with inter-lamellar spacing below 100 nm.
The refined fcc/B2 interfaces will be coherent.
Severe deformation breaks down coarse lamellae and increases phase-boundary density.
Subsequent annealing at 600–700 °C stabilizes a fine lamellar pattern without causing coarsening.
Coherent interfaces allow dislocations to shear the hard B2 phase and transmit into the soft fcc phase rather than accumulating at interfaces.
Dislocation transmission across phase boundaries will relieve interfacial stress concentrations and arrest cracking.
Fine lamellar spacing increases strain hardening by storing dislocations in the soft phase, thereby delaying necking and catastrophic failure.
The treatment will produce an ultimate tensile strength above 1.2 GPa together with elongation above 20% at room temperature.
The fracture mode will change from interfacial cleavage to ductile micro-void coalescence.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a room-temperature fracture strength of about 944 MPa and engineering elongation of about 25.6%.
Successful refinement is limited to 900–1000 °C, where dynamic recrystallization occurs without excessive grain growth or phase decomposition.
Above 1100 °C, the lamellar structure may coarsen or dissolve into a lower-strength single-phase structure.
Below 200 MPa, lamellar refinement and formation of the patterned structure will not occur.
HIP at approximately 1200 °C and 150 MPa for 4 hours can induce secondary-phase formation in a high-entropy alloy.
Conventional HIP may produce brittle HCP or Laves-like secondary phases and ductility below 10% in AlCoCrFeNi.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as having low ductility and catastrophic early failure, while the cited-composition baseline is assigned 25.6% elongation, which is comparatively ductile. The baseline hedges that the actual target may be lower, but the target composition is not specified sufficiently to resolve the discrepancy.
